title: QD-PINN: 1D Shiryaev quickest-detection free boundary
setting: The posterior probability pi of a change point follows a 1D diffusion with hazard rate 1, signal-to-noise rho = 1/sigma^2, running cost c*pi and terminal penalty 1-pi. This gives a free-boundary variational inequality min{LV + c*pi, (1-pi) - V} = 0. A small tanh MLP for V plus a learnable scalar boundary s is trained for 200 Adam steps on random collocation points, using PDE, value-matching, smooth-fit and (optionally) Fischer-Burmeister complementarity losses. The baseline is a finite-difference policy-iteration solver whose number of grid nodes equals the collocation count. Both are scored against a fine-grid (800-node) finite-difference reference boundary.

paper.title: QD-PINN: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach to Bayesian Quickest Detection in High-Dimensional Diffusions
paper.claim: A PINN with a complementarity-enforcing unified loss recovers the optimal stopping boundary of the quickest-detection free-boundary problem in close agreement with reference numerical solutions.

metric.name: boundary_abs_error
metric.description: Absolute error of the estimated stopping boundary pi* (stop when posterior >= pi*) against the fine-grid finite-difference reference boundary. Diagnostics: value_mae (mean abs error of V on 200 held-out points), pi_star, ref_boundary.

factors.name: method
factors.description: fd_coarse: finite-difference policy iteration on a grid with n_col nodes (traditional baseline). pinn_qd: PINN with the full loss including max/min and Fischer-Burmeister complementarity terms. pinn_no_complementarity: the same PINN without the complementarity terms (ablation).

factors.name: c
factors.description: Running delay cost rate; moves the true boundary from near 1 (low c) to small values (high c).

factors.name: sigma
factors.description: Observation noise scale; signal-to-noise rho = 1/sigma^2 sets the diffusion strength of the posterior and the curvature of V.

factors.name: n_col
factors.description: Collocation points for the PINN, and the matched number of grid nodes for the finite-difference baseline.
